name: preview_revert
description: What reverting one change, one run, or one task (across agents) would do, without doing it: each row the revert would restore (RESTORE) and each row it would leave alone because someone changed it after the agent (SKIP, with the reason). People win: a skipped row is never overwritten. The preview runs the revert on trial and rolls it back. Nothing is reverted here: only a person can revert, with their passkey. To hand them a revert of one of your own changes or runs, call request_revert (it returns a link to show them); otherwise they run the returned command. Name exactly one of changeId, runId, taskId. Lines are cursor-paginated in their signed order. Any size can be previewed; a revert over 1000 lines becomes a plan the agent applies in batches after the person signs it (revert_plan, apply_revert_batch).

changeId.description: Revert one change (a revert's own changeId reverts that revert).

runId.description: Revert every applied change of one run.

taskId.description: Revert every applied change of one task, by any agent.

rows.description: RESTORE lines in the whole preview.

skipped.description: SKIP lines in the whole preview.

command.description: The command the person runs to revert, e.g. basalt revert --run <runId>.

op.description: The inverse write the revert would run.

now.description: The row as it is now. Absent when redacted.

set.description: The values the revert would write. Absent when redacted.

redacted.description: True when this agent cannot SELECT the table; key and values are hidden.

nextSteps.description: Planned (CONTRACT.md, Next steps): what to do next, first step first.

personMessage.description: Planned (CONTRACT.md, Next steps): one plain line the agent shows the person verbatim.
